lines: I.  Introduction

A scalar query measures q coordinates and must distinguish the truth from an alternative. The corpus states its per-sample information against an alternative parameterised by (d, x): d coordinates displaced by μ, the remaining q − d displaced by x.

Two objections stand against using that statement. First, a bound proved only over a two-parameter SLICE says nothing about alternatives outside it, so a lower bound quantified over (d, x) is not a lower bound over the class. Second, the design weights that reproduce the corpus's coefficients were FITTED — a consistent non-negative solution in 24 of 24 parameter cells is evidence that the coefficients come from the model, but it is not a derivation.
This work removes both objections. Neither is answered by more cells or more search; each needs an argument.

III.  Results

THE DERIVED WEIGHTS MATCH ALL 24 CELLS EXACTLY. Across q ∈ {8, 16}, μ ∈ {1/4, 2/5}, c ∈ {3/2, 2} and η ∈ {1/3, 13/20, 4/5}, the fitted weights agree with the derived formula in every cell, and the budget identity holds exactly in each. The weights vary with (η, c) and are constant across (q, μ), exactly as the derivation predicts.
THE SEPARATION IS CERTIFIED ON EVERY CELL TESTED. Eight of eight cells certify the strict separation across the whole cell, all of them by the left-endpoint test, with exact rational gaps.

THE PAIR QUERY IS NECESSARY WHEREVER IT IS USED. On 20 parameter cells the A-pair carries positive weight in 17, and in all 17 its necessity is certified: the full value strictly exceeds the best value achievable without it. The three cells without a certificate are exactly those where the pair weight is zero, so nothing is missing — the query is simply not used there.

Fig. 2.  Where the necessity construction breaks, against the margin. The curves rise monotonically; at rho = 2 no breakdown occurs anywhere on the grid.
IV.  Discussion

THE NECESSITY CONSTRUCTION DOES NOT COLLAPSE OFF THE CORNER — IT DEGRADES. Sufficiency is proved for every product reference, necessity only at the corner, and nothing in the development says what happens between. An exact rational sweep, validated against the proved identity at t = 0 before anything was reported, shows the witness weakening continuously and failing only past a breakdown point that RISES with the margin: at n = 8 from 5/32 at μ = 1 to 7/16 at μ = 7/4. IT IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF THE PATH CHOSEN. The first sweep moved the reference symmetrically, which is the direction the construction is symmetric in. Widened to asymmetric references drawn independently per coordinate, the Top-C set is lost MORE often, 49.6% against 41.2%, and the four structured directions less often, 18.0%. The symmetric path sits inside the range the others span, so reading it as representative is licensed by measurement. SUFFICIENCY SURVIVES EVERYTHING TESTED. At μ = 2 the Top-C set is retained at every one of 903 references — symmetric, structured and asymmetric — and the regret is non-positive at every t > 0. That cannot confirm a theorem proved for all references, but it exercises it where the necessity construction lives.
Fig. 3.  How often Top-C is lost, by the direction the reference moves in. The symmetric path sits inside the range the other directions span.
V.  Conclusions

The two-parameter alternative family is not a restriction, the design is not fitted, and the margin at which Top-C selection stops being optimal is sharp at 2δ. Sufficiency holds under every product reference; necessity is proved at the corner, and measured to survive a neighbourhood of it whose size grows with the margin. The honest summary is narrower than this work first claimed and broader than the theorem states: the construction degrades rather than collapses, and at the threshold margin no reference tested defeats it.
How the numbers were produced

EVERY DEFINITION IS TRANSCRIBED, NOT RE-DERIVED. The gate, the coefficient map, the steered world and the compression loss come from the formal sources rather than being rebuilt for the experiment — an earlier version invented its own construction and produced a confident, wrong answer. THE TRANSCRIPTION IS VALIDATED AT THE ONE POINT THE THEOREMS APPLY. At t = 0 it must reproduce the proved oscillation profile and the proved exchange identity, doubled regret exactly |A|(2−ρ), before any swept result is reported. It does, in every configuration. EXACT RATIONALS THROUGHOUT, so a reported flip is a flip and not a rounding artefact, and the breakdown point is located to 1/64 rather than estimated. Unbalanced configurations are swept in a separate arm precisely BECAUSE the exchange identity does not cover them, and nothing there is checked against it.
